asr_text: I'm for a rule at my daughter's high school that keeps phones off during breaks and lunch too. Banning them only during class isn't enough. I get home late from the job site, and fighting about phones every night is exhausting. If I could say, "That's the rule at school too," then I don't have to be the only bad guy. My daughter didn't keep our agreement to put her phone in the charging basket in the living room. The morning after I took it away, it was hard to talk to her at breakfast. She also said, if I'm the only one who replies late, I'll be left out. I had no answer for that. I want her to stick to what we've agreed. I don't want to yell like my father either. But even if she can't use her phone at school during the day, nothing changes at home at night. Maybe I just want to ask the school for help so things are easier for me. I'm a site supervisor who can't even get things organized at home.
